qb_passing_yards.rederivation_notes: My own chain, written before reading the record: QB1 availability and snap scenarios (full game, injury exit, blowout bench, backup start); team plays from both tempos; pass rate over expected rewritten by score path; dropbacks minus sacks, scrambles and spikes give attempts (individual passing yards are gross); completions times yards per completion with depth, YAC, pressure and coverage; weather and one long play for the right tail; settlement by N+ rung (floor_strike N-0.5), protected first-half refund, H2H 50/50 and fair-price void, weekly-most 1/N. Required inputs: QB status vintage, pace, PROE, script, opponent run defence, pressure and line, receiver availability, weather, explosive rate, exit and bench hazard. The record's stages match closely and its new inputs are good. Differences: no mechanism for the season, career and weekly-most tickers (3 of 7 live series); spread_line and total_line feed nfl.script; a duplicate-audited input is still used in stage s4; no run-game term; inactive-QB settlement not covered by the text. All quoted evidence was checked verbatim and is correct; overtime is rightly left ambiguous.

findings.text: Three of seven live series are not per-game contracts and have no stage, input or data: KXNFLSEASONPASSYDS, KXNFLCAREERPASSYDS and KXNFLWEEKMOSTPASSYDS (league-wide max over QBs, non-participant resolves No). Stages s1-s7 are all single-game and no unresolved entry discloses this. The season_player_stats_and_leaders record holds the needed inputs but has no live series, so these tickers have no attached input list.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: added contract.series_mapping_issues mapping KXNFLSEASONPASSYDS, KXNFLCAREERPASSYDS and KXNFLWEEKMOSTPASSYDS to season_player_stats_and_leaders, rewrote settlement_definition and variants so the record claims only per-game contracts.

findings.text: Market-derived values are listed as raw data: the 'Weather, roof and schedule context' dataset has spread_line and total_line fields feeding nfl.script. These are sportsbook lines. The record never says script must be built from own ratings, so the input is a market echo as written.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: removed spread_line/total_line from the weather/schedule dataset, added market-free new input nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior to stage s3 and re-audited nfl.script so its margin distribution comes from own EPA ratings.

findings.text: nfl.pass_rush is audited DUPLICATE_OF:nfl.pressure_qb but remains an input of stage s4, of opponent_matchup coverage and of an interaction. Duplicates should be removed from stages and interactions.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: removed duplicate nfl.pass_rush from stage s4, opponent_matchup coverage, the interaction list and dataset feeds; nfl.pressure_qb carries the pressure matchup.

findings.text: Dropback volume has no run-game term (opponent run defence, own rushing efficiency), although nfl.run_defense exists in the catalog and sibling archetypes use it.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: attached nfl.run_defense and nfl.rush_efficiency to stage s2 and pace_volume coverage with a note that run-game quality sets dropback conversion of neutral plays.

findings.text: The PRECISE text only covers a QB who is 'active but never takes a snap'. The treatment of an inactive QB is not stated, yet the record presents the void rule as settled. This should be a CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS entry.

The free nflverse field list includes was_pressure and time_to_throw, but unresolved u2 says free play-by-play does not contain pressure and time to throw reliably. The two statements conflict; availability by season is unverified (the nflverse dictionary could not be reached from this session).

The interaction on proe, script and pace restates dropbacks = plays x pass rate, and the def_epa/pass_rush/qb_efficiency diminishing-returns item is really about script. The H2H contract needs the correlation between two QBs' totals but no input or interaction provides it.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: replaced the proe/script/pace identity with a PROE-by-deficit conditional interaction, rewrote the efficiency interaction around pressure, and added a two-QB joint-distribution interaction with nfl.corr for the H2H contract.

receiving_yards_and_receptions.rederivation_notes: My own chain: receiver active and route participation (snap share, return caps, exit); team dropback pool from pace, PROE, script and run defence; QB identity and accuracy scaling every receiver; targets per route run with alignment, competition and redistribution when a teammate is out; coverage, shadowing and target funnel; catch probability and yards per catch; long-play tail and longest reception as a max of N catches; payoff shapes (N+ rung, linear ladder capped at 20 receptions or 400 yards, cubic escalators capped at 14 receptions or 200 yards bucketed in tens, longest-reception strike, H2H, protected). Required inputs: routes, TPRR, teammate-out matrix, QB status, pace/PROE/script, coverage matchup, weather, length distribution. The record matches stages 1-7 and its payoff analysis is accurate (formulas and quotes verified). Differences: QB starter status and receiver exit risk are not attached; nfl.pace is admitted as not attached though pace_volume is COVERED; nfl.corr is cited but never audited; routes are claimed free but u2 says they are not; the escalator convexity claim ignores the cap.

findings.text: Quarterback availability is missing: no nfl.qb or nfl.in_game_exit_risk input in any stage; nfl.qb_efficiency appears only as an accuracy term in s5. A backup QB start is the largest shift in every receiver's volume, and the protected variant keys on the receiver's own in-game exit.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: added nfl.qb, nfl.in_game_exit_risk and nfl.pace to stages s1/s2, availability_news coverage and the injury dataset feeds; stage s2 text now describes backup-QB regime and the protected-variant exit.

findings.text: Coverage is overstated: pace_volume is COVERED with only nfl.proe while its note says nfl.pace 'is not attached here'; distribution_variance lists nfl.corr although its note says it is not attached, and nfl.corr is never audited or used. Acknowledged omissions are shown as coverage.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: attached nfl.pace to s2 and pace_volume coverage, attached nfl.corr to s6 with play-level feed, and rewrote both coverage notes so no omitted input is shown as covered.

findings.text: Primary-input data claim is contradictory: the play-level dataset lists routes-run flag and alignment as free nflverse fields, but u2 says free play-by-play lacks routes run. nfl.routes and the TPRR inputs are primary, so access (free or paid, which seasons) is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED and must be labelled so.

The escalator payoffs are convex only below the cap; at 14 receptions or 200 yards they go flat, so more variance can lower value for high-volume receivers. The variance interaction says variance 'increases fair value' without this, and uses an input audited WEAK.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: rewrote the escalator variance interaction as piecewise, stating the payoff is convex only below the 14-reception/200-yard cap and flat above it, and replaced the WEAK nfl.player_stat_variance-only framing with the reception-length distribution.

findings.text: Weekly-most, season, career, record and rush-plus-receive tickers share this key with different mechanisms; u3 discloses it but defines no inputs for them.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: added series_mapping_issues for six season/career/record/weekly-most tickers (to season_player_stats_and_leaders) and KXNFLRRYDS (new archetype needed) and limited the settlement text to per-game contracts.

findings.text: The claim that a longest-reception contract settles at zero for a player with a live play but no catch is an inference; the text only says it settles on the longest reception recorded. It should be CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

rushing_yards.rederivation_notes: My own chain: who carries (lead back or committee share by down and goal line, QB designed runs and scrambles); health, snap ramp and exit hazard with carries passing to the next back; team rush plays = plays x run rate set by pace, PROE and score path; yards per carry from blocking, front and box, scheme and runner; explosive tail; QB rushing as a separate process; settlement: protected first-half refund, H2H 50/50 with void, game-most and week-most as maxima over a field with 1/N and non-participant No, season totals. Required inputs: carry share, availability and limited-snap discount, exit hazard, run defence and line, script, PROE and pace, weather, explosive rate, QB rushing, plus whole-field projections for the max contracts. The record's seven stages match and its additions are good. Differences: no field inputs for game-most and week-most; season and career tickers have no mechanism; duplicate-audited inputs remain in stages; some interaction mechanisms are speculative. All quotes verified.

findings.text: Max-of-field contracts have no inputs: KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS (all players in the game, non-participant No, 1/N ties) and KXNFLWEEKMOSTRSHYDS need projections and joint distributions for every rusher on both teams or league-wide. Stages model a single runner and no field-projection input or dataset exists (compare the fantasy record's weekly field grid).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: game-most mapped to NEW_ARCHETYPE_NEEDED single_game_stat_leader_field_max and weekly-most to season_player_stats_and_leaders in series_mapping_issues; settlement text now limited to per-game runner contracts.

findings.text: Season and career tickers (KXNFLSEASONRSHYDS, KXNFLSEASONRUSHYDS, KXNFLCAREERRSHYDS) are filed here but the chain is per-game: no games-played hazard, banked total, role-regime or age horizon is attached and no unresolved entry says so. The two season tickers look like spelling duplicates and the mapping was not checked.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: season and career tickers recorded in series_mapping_issues under season_player_stats_and_leaders, claims restricted to per-game chain; the possible spelling duplicate is carried as unresolved u5.

findings.text: nfl.garbage_time is DUPLICATE_OF:nfl.script yet stays in s4 and coverage; nfl.player_stat_variance is audited WEAK yet stays in s6, coverage and an interaction.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: removed nfl.garbage_time (duplicate of script) and WEAK nfl.player_stat_variance from stage s4/s6, coverage, feeds and the compounding interaction, now keyed on carries and explosive-tail rate.

findings.text: The protected-variant evidence 'establishes' that overtime is included for statistics, but the truncated text only counts overtime participation as after the first half. Whether overtime yards count is unstated; a player with no first-half play under the protected rule is not addressed.

The weather/proe/rush_efficiency interaction asserts zone-power offences gain and finesse runs lose with no evidence; mark MECHANISM_UNCERTAIN. defenders_in_box and was_pressure are listed as free nflverse fields while u2 says box counts are only partly free; availability is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: weather/run-style interaction text reduced to a hypothesis with new unresolved u7 (MECHANISM_UNCERTAIN); defenders_in_box and was_pressure fields labelled unverified with new unresolved u8 (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

findings.text: Rushing attempts is in the archetype label but KXNFLRSHATT is filed under the specials key; neither record models attempts, so they fall between archetypes.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: recorded KXNFLRSHATT in series_mapping_issues as belonging to rushing_yards, whose carry-share and team rush-play stages (s1-s4, nfl.carries) are its volume mechanism; the specials record must attach it there.

season_awards.rederivation_notes: My own chain: an award is a vote by a bounded panel (about 50 AP voters for annual awards; a league process for monthly awards) over an eligibility-filtered pool. Stages: eligibility (rookie, side of ball, month window); production as voters see it (counting stats, milestones, sacks and interceptions for defence, QB bias for MVP); team success; availability before the ballot closes; narrative and exposure; vote aggregation with teammate splitting; award-specific drivers (coach surprise, comeback severity, 3-5 game monthly windows). Draft, Hall of Fame, All-Pro and finalist markets are different mechanisms and should be separate. Required inputs: candidate production projection for offence and defence, standings simulation, games-played hazard, historical voting data, ballot timing. The record covers the vote chain well. Differences: the production stage rests on WEAK or QB-only inputs with no defensive production input; about 20 of 40 live series are draft markets with no mechanism; the settlement text misdescribes the series mix; the month window is inferred. Quotes verified.

findings.text: Most live series are not season awards: about 20 are NFL Draft markets (KXNFLDRAFT1, FIRSTPICK, DRAFTPICK, DRAFTSELECT, DRAFTOU, DRAFTTEAM, position-drafted series, LASTPICKPOS, supplemental draft series and others) plus Hall of Fame, All-Pro, All-Rookie, finalists and an interception leader. No draft board, team-needs, mock-consensus or trade input exists here. u2 admits this and recommends splitting, but the split was not done, so about half the live series have no usable input list.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: listed 20 Draft tickers, two Hall of Fame tickers and KXNFLLEADERPINT in contract.series_mapping_issues with their correct archetype, rewrote settlement_definition and variants so this record claims only the season-award votes.

findings.text: The production-vs-peers stage s2 uses only inputs the record audits as WEAK (nfl.award_stats, nfl.fantasy_points_model) or QB-specific (nfl.qb_efficiency), and no new input replaces them. There is no defensive-production input (sacks, pressures, interceptions) for DPOY/DROY, no cross-position index for OPOY and no rest-of-season stat projection. The note that milestone and exposure inputs replace award_stats is unsupported.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: added new inputs nfl.position_peer_production_index (offence EPA plus defensive sack/pressure/INT/TFL composite) and nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection, removed WEAK award_stats and fantasy_points_model from stage s2 and coverage, updated interactions and data feeds.

findings.text: settlement_definition says 38 of 40 series are draft, Hall of Fame and finalist markets with no rules sampled. Only 2 have rules; the other 38 include true awards (MVP, OPOY, DPOY, OROY, COTY, CPOTY), so the mix is misdescribed.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: rewrote settlement_definition to say 2 of 40 series have rules text, and that of the other 38 about 14 are true award markets, about 20 Draft markets and the rest HOF, All-Pro, finalist and leader markets.

findings.text: The monthly window is asserted to be a fixed calendar month and nfl.award_month_window_games counts 3-5 games from the schedule, but the text only says 'for October'. Calendar versus week-block definition is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS and affects a primary input.

The td_luck/exposure item states how voters behave rather than an interaction of two inputs, and the split-penalty interaction uses two WEAK inputs. Ballot format for MVP (ranked points versus plurality) is unverified.

Straw-poll capture is manual with no cited structured archive; scraping terms for Pro-Football-Reference are unchecked; per-voter ballots are mostly not public, which limits the split-penalty fit to vote totals.

season_player_stats_and_leaders.rederivation_notes: My own chain, derived from the family list and sibling season tickers since no series is mapped: season total = banked to date plus the sum over remaining games of P(play) x per-game rate. Stages: banked total and games remaining (byes, 17 games in 18 weeks); availability hazard with clustered absences and late clinched-team rest; role state with regime-change risk; team volume and efficiency; touchdown regression; variance of the sum with within-season persistence; leaders as maxima over correlated contenders with an open field; weekly leaders as single-game maxima over the whole pool; settlement hazards (regular season only, no void for missed games, 1/N dead heat, stat source). The record contains all of these and its stages are sound. Differences: nothing can be verified against rules text; the live season tickers sit in other archetypes that do not attach these inputs; one input is labelled duplicate yet still used; one interaction is not an interaction; a transactions source is claimed free and unavailable at once; team-level stats in the stated target are not covered.

findings.text: No live series is mapped while season-total tickers exist under qb_passing_yards, receiving, rushing_yards and the fantasy key, whose records do not attach this record's inputs (games played, role-regime hazard, rate persistence, clinch rest, contender covariance). The inputs are required by live contracts but belong to no archetype that prices them; u1 discloses the unmapped state but not this consequence.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: contract.series_mapping_issues now lists 14 live season, career, weekly-most and leader tickers filed under four other archetypes that need this record's inputs, and u1 and settlement_definition state the consequence.

findings.text: nfl.skill_avail is DUPLICATE_OF:nfl.role_regime_change_hazard yet remains in stage s2, coverage and data feeds. Observable teammate injury status is not the same quantity as a forecast hazard of role shift, so the verdict looks wrong and the stage disagrees with the audit.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: changed nfl.skill_avail audit from DUPLICATE_OF to KEEP_SECONDARY, with reason that observed teammate status is a trigger feeding the role-regime hazard, matching its place in stage s2.

findings.text: The td_luck/season_to_date_pace item concludes the remaining rate is role-based regardless of banked touchdowns, i.e. it asserts no interaction. The contender-covariance text about QB-receiver covariance is muddled and needs a sign and a test.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: replaced the no-interaction td_luck item with a td_luck x role-regime hazard conditional interaction with a test, and rewrote the contender covariance mechanism with explicit signs (positive same-team passing pairs, negative same-position teammates) and a Brier test.

findings.text: The availability dataset lists 'nflverse injuries, rosters and transactions' as free, but u4 says transaction and coaching-change timelines are not available as a clean free dataset. A nflverse transactions table is not known to exist; the primary role_regime_change_hazard input would need manual curation.

The stated target includes teams and head-to-head, and families include team leader, matchup and team event, but all stages are player-based. ICC 0.1-0.3 and the 25 percent shift threshold are assumptions (disclosed in u2).

season_win_totals_and_futures.rederivation_notes: My own chain: latent team strength with shared preseason uncertainty (prior from last year, roster continuity, QB change, coaching change) updated by opponent-adjusted results; QB and key-player availability scenarios; game win probability from rating difference, home field and rest; ties possible (about 0.2-0.3 percent per game, half win in standings); a season simulation conditional on games already played (it is Week 9) giving the win-count pmf; division and seed through the full tiebreak ladder; bracket with one bye per conference; special futures (first pick via bottom of standings, draft tiebreak and pick trades; undefeated; round qualifiers; exact pairing; combos). Required inputs: own rating with posterior sd, QB scenario tree, schedule graph, tiebreak rules, bracket mapping, injury vintage, pick ownership. Market lines are benchmarks only. The record matches this structure and adds good inputs. Differences: nfl.ratings is WEAK and market-mixed with no own-rating construction; a benchmark-only input is in stage s7; the bye question for KXNFLROUNDQUAL is an undisclosed ambiguity; spread_line and win probability are raw rating fields; Super Bowl MVP and several sidecar tickers have no inputs; one formula mixes sd and variance. Quotes verified.

findings.text: The core input is unspecified: nfl.ratings is audited WEAK (mixes own ratings with market-implied history) yet stays in stage s1 and talent_strength coverage, and no new input defines the own rating (opponent-adjusted model, window, home-field constant, preseason prior). The game-results dataset also lists spread_line and win probability as fields feeding nfl.ratings and nfl.schedule_strength, which are market-derived. Every contract here depends on the rating, so the list cannot be relied on until it is defined without market values.

Undisclosed ambiguity: KXNFLROUNDQUAL ('qualifies for the divisional round') has only a primary rule. Whether the #1 seed, which has a bye and plays no wild-card game, counts as qualified is not stated; it changes P(contract) by P(1 seed). u1 covers only win-total ties.
nfl.futures_coherence is BENCHMARK_ONLY yet is an input of stage s7; nfl.season_sim_distribution is DUPLICATE_OF:nfl.standings_sim yet used in s4 and coverage.

Sidecar tickers lack inputs: Super Bowl MVP (KXNFLSBMVP, SBMVPQB, SBMVPDEF, SBMVPPOS), KXNFLSZNRECORD, division most/least wins, wins by week, playoff host, seed over/under and multi-year KXNFLENDSTREAK. u5 discloses this but the archetype was not split; the KXNFLNBA combo needs an NBA leg outside any NFL input list.

Quantitative slips: the posterior sd formula treats 'residual sd 13.5' as a variance; the preseason sd of 2.2 rating points looks low; the tie rate is about 0.2 percent here and 0.25 percent in the specials record. Use one calibrated value.

The shared-error by standings_sim interaction is structural, not a feature interaction. The requirement that the simulation be conditioned on games already played and current injuries is implied but not stated.

team_total.rederivation_notes: My own chain: team points = sum over own drives of discrete scores (TD plus conversion, FG, nothing) plus defensive and special-teams scores and safeties; drives available from both teams' pace and ball control; start position and special teams; drive outcome from own offence against the opposing defence (pass and run separately); kicker range, fourth-down and two-point policy; QB, line and skill availability; weather; score path; overtime only if tied. Contract: KXNFLTEAMTOTAL is a strict over on one team's score (text silent on overtime and postponement); KXNFLBOTH counts overtime and has the 48-hour rule. Output should be the integer pmf with key numbers and the joint with the opponent for KXNFLBOTH. Required inputs: pass/run-split offence and defence ratings, drives, both paces, red zone, kicker, QB status, weather, field position, 4th-down policy, non-offensive scoring, a joint score model. The record matches and adds good inputs. Differences: market-derived inputs remain in stage s7 and coverage; pass/run decomposition inputs are marked duplicate although its interaction needs them; the overtime figures are off; the joint with the opponent is undefined. Quotes verified.

findings.text: Market-derived inputs stay in stages and coverage: nfl.team_total_split (BENCHMARK_ONLY, market-derived by construction) is an input of s7 and the only support listed for distribution_variance; nfl.score_resid is kept although defined around market lines; the market-lines dataset feeds team_total_split. Flagging does not make a benchmark an input; s7 needs an own compound score distribution.

nfl.coverage_scheme, nfl.run_defense and nfl.pass_rush are all DUPLICATE_OF:nfl.def_epa, yet interaction 1 says a pass-heavy offence suffers more against a strong pass defence and a run-heavy one against a strong run defence, which needs separate pass and run EPA for both sides. Collapsing to one def_epa removes what the interaction needs, and the duplicates are still listed in s3.

The overtime figure 'roughly 0.5-1 point to each team's expected total ... conditional on a tied regulation' is unsupported and ambiguous; unconditionally overtime adds roughly 0.1-0.2 points per team (about 6 percent of games). KXNFLTEAMTOTAL overtime is unknown while KXNFLBOTH counts it, so the pmf truncation differs.
The bivariate score model for KXNFLBOTH is not an input (u2 admits it); add score covariance through pace, script and weather. Home-field and venue are absent as inputs.

nfl.drives, nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial, nfl.pace and drive_result_lattice overlap in estimating possessions and efficiency; this duplication is not audited. The 4-7 point backup-QB loss is unsourced.

Kicker, non-offensive scoring and fourth-down inputs rely on nflFastR flags (td_team, safety, fourth_down_converted, two_point_attempt); current-season availability and the quote-time availability vintage (u3) are unverified.

unreg:fantasy_points_markets.rederivation_notes: My own chain: fantasy points are a linear combination of components under Sleeper scoring (passing yard 0.04, passing TD 4, interception -1, rush and receiving yard 0.1, reception 1, TD 6, fumble lost, kicker field goals by distance, defence and special teams). Stages: participation atom at zero (non-play scores 0, not void); opportunity by position (QB dropbacks and rushes, RB carries and targets, WR/TE targets); yield with opponent and weather; touchdown luck from expected TDs by location; negative events; component covariance and team stacks; order statistics (weekly leader over the whole pool, top-N dead heat, any-game maxima, season totals and H2H); settlement on Sleeper's number at expiration with Sleeper-defined groups. Required inputs: for every position including QB, kicker and D/ST, opportunity, availability, xTD, matchup, weather, pace and script, covariance, field projections, plus season inputs for season-long tickers. The record is strong on aggregation, xTD, stack covariance and the field grid. Differences: no quarterback chain; no kicker or defence inputs although the sampled single-game ticker is a kicker; opponent matchup is a declared GAP; environment is declared not applicable; season-long tickers lack season inputs. Quotes verified.

findings.text: No quarterback mechanism: no nfl.qb, qb_efficiency, qb_rushing or dropback input appears anywhere in the record, although scoring gives passing yards 0.04, passing TD 4 and QB rushing full rushing value. Live tickers include KXNFLFFH2HSEASON (sample: Lamar Jackson vs Josh Allen), position leaders and weekly leaders whose pools include QBs. Stage s2 lists only targets and carries, and the field grid has a QB pool but no component model for it.

Kicker and defence/special-teams scoring have no inputs although the sampled per-game ticker KXNFLFFPTS is Will Reichard (strike 9.2). u2 discloses it, but s5 lists only nfl.fantasy_points_model and nfl.pace; nfl.kicker, nfl.redzone, nfl.drives and long-FG inputs from sibling records are not attached. The text is truncated before the kicker table, and the Weeks 15-17 leader excludes kickers and D/ST while KXNFLFFPTS includes them.

Category declarations are wrong for the single-game tickers: environment is NOT_APPLICABLE citing season and ranking contracts, but KXNFLFFPTS, KXNFLFFPTSLADDER, the weekly leader markets and any-game highs are single games sensitive to wind, roof and cold. opponent_matchup is a GAP although nfl.def_epa, nfl.coverage_scheme, nfl.cb_coverage_matchup, nfl.run_defense and nfl.dvp exist in the catalog and are used by sibling archetypes.

Season-long tickers (season total, season H2H, position leader and top-N) and the Weeks 15-17 leader need banked totals, games-played hazard, role-regime hazard and late-season rest; only nfl.games_played_dist is attached. situational_schedule_motivation is COVERED by a grid input whose note says it does not model clinch rest.

Settlement claims generalise single sentences: 'corrections after expiration are not considered' and 'including overtime' appear in some series' text only but are stated for all eleven; the ladder says 'standard Points Per Reception' while others say full-PPR, a wording variant to confirm. VERIFIED_FROM_RULES_TEXT is too strong given the truncated scoring table.

The targets/fantasy_points_model diminishing-returns item is a response curve of targets, not an interaction, and pairs it with a specification input. Interceptions and fumbles lost have no inputs, and the field grid's 'projected total' has no stated source (a market total would be a benchmark).

unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials.rederivation_notes: My own chain, after splitting this grab-bag first. (A) Per-game team counts (field goals, sacks, yards, race to 35): opportunities x per-opportunity rate under score path and weather, overdispersed; race-to-N is a first-passage on both scores including overtime. (B) The player prop KXNFLRSHATT needs carry share, availability and team rush plays. (C) Season futures that are functions of the standings simulation: ties, win streak, last undefeated, division order, worst-to-first, stage of elimination, championship matchup, fewest or most points scored and allowed (needs separate offence and defence scoring rates), week's highest-scoring team (max over 32 teams). (D) Non-game: primetime count, Top 100 voted list, next-interception window. Season contracts must be conditioned on games already played (Week 9). Required inputs: for A the usual; for C own ratings with shared error, offence/defence split, tie rate, tiebreaks, bracket and banked state; for D schedule, flex and voter inputs. The record handles A well and gives a stylised simulator for part of C. Differences: no inputs for most of B, C and D; a simulator duplicating the win-totals record; no banked-state conditioning; inconsistent tie statements. Quotes verified.

findings.text: About half of the 19 live series have no stage or input: KXNFLSTAGEOFELIM, KXNFLMATCHUP, KXNFLDIVISIONORDER, KXNFLWORSTTOFIRST (need the standings, tiebreak and bracket simulation), KXNFLTEAMPTS and KXNFLTEAMDPTS (need separate offence and defence scoring rates; a single margin rating cannot give points for and against), KXNFLWEEKHIGHSCORE (max over 32 team scores), KXNFLT100TOP (s7 says 'non-game inputs' but defines none), KXNFLNEXTINT and KXNFLRSHATT (s1 has only pace, drives and script, no carry share or availability). u1 says they are 'only mentioned, not modelled' but they are live; the group should be split and each family attached to the right chain.

nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path re-specifies a 272-game simulation (rating sd 2.2, tie 0.25 percent per game) parallel to nfl.standings_sim and nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error in the win-totals record, and says 'simulate the 272-game season' without conditioning on games already played. It is Week 9, so KXNFLLASTTOLOSE, KXNFLWINSTREAK, KXNFLTIES and KXNFL60YARDFGS are partly decided by banked results. Required inputs must include current season state and one shared simulator.
